name: British Columbia
note: British Columbia provincial roles for incapacity, death and estate administration: enduring and general powers of attorney, representation agreements, temporary substitute decision makers, committees and statutory property guardians, executors and administrators under WESA, organ donation consent, control of disposition of remains, and access to a deceased person's records. Statutes as consolidated on bclaws.gov.bc.ca, current to 15 September 2026 (Supreme Court Civil Rules current to 8 September 2026). Federal roles (CPP/OAS trustees, CRA, PIPEDA, ULCC) are in ca-federal.

roles.name: Attorney under an enduring power of attorney
roles.summary: An adult (19 or older) names an attorney to manage financial affairs, and the document must say the authority continues despite incapability. It can take effect as soon as it is signed, or on a stated date or confirmed event such as incapability. It ends on the adult's death, revocation, a court order, a Patients Property Act committee order, or events affecting the attorney.

assigned.event: Capable adult signs the enduring power of attorney before 2 witnesses (or 1 lawyer or notary witness)

starts.event: Latest of: signing by both the adult and the attorney, a stated effective date, or confirmation of a stated triggering event (e.g. incapability confirmed as the document directs, or by a qualified health care provider if the named person cannot act)

ends.event: Adult dies
Adult revokes (while capable) and gives written notice to each attorney
Court terminates the enduring power of attorney under s 36(5)

Adult becomes a patient by court declaration under the Patients Property Act (terminated), or a statutory property guardianship begins and the Public Guardian and Trustee decides to manage the property (suspended, then terminated)

The attorney's authority ends: attorney resigns, dies, becomes incapable or bankrupt, is convicted of a prescribed offence or one against the adult, or is the adult's spouse and they separate (unless the document says otherwise)

states.label: Signed by the adult but not yet effective (the attorney has not signed, or the stated date or event has not arrived or been confirmed)
Attorney may act on the adult's financial affairs
Suspended under circumstances stated in the document, or under Patients Property Act s 19.1 pending the Public Guardian and Trustee's decision

transitions.event: Adult signs before witnesses
conditions: Adult understands the matters in s 12(2)
Document states whether the attorney may act while the adult is capable or only while incapable, and that authority continues despite incapability

transitions.event: Attorney signs before 2 witnesses and no later effective date or triggering event is stated
Stated triggering event (e.g. incapability) is confirmed by the person and method named in the document
conditions: If the named person cannot or will not confirm incapability, a qualified health care provider may confirm it

transitions.event: Adult becomes incapable
conditions: Authority continues; attorney may act despite the incapable adult's objections, subject to s 19 duties

transitions.event: Circumstances stated in the document arise, or a certificate of incapability makes the adult a patient (Patients Property Act s 19.1)
Suspending circumstances end, or the Public Guardian and Trustee decides it need not manage the property
Capable adult revokes and gives written notice
conditions: Effective when notice given or on a later stated date

transitions.event: Court declares the adult a patient under the Patients Property Act, or PGT decides to manage property after a certificate of incapability
Attorney resigns, dies, becomes incapable or bankrupt, or spousal relationship with the adult ends
conditions: Remaining attorneys may continue unless the document says otherwise
Separation rule does not apply if the document says authority continues

transitions.event: Adult dies

notes.text: Adult bankruptcy is not listed in Power of Attorney Act s 30 as ending an enduring power of attorney. Only the attorney's bankruptcy (s 29(2)(d)(iii)) is listed. A government-hosted seniors' guide says both types of POA end on the donor's bankruptcy; that rests on general law, not on the text of the Act.
An enduring power of attorney made outside BC that continues during incapacity may be treated as a BC enduring power of attorney, subject to regulations.

roles.name: Attorney under a general (non-enduring) power of attorney
roles.summary: A general power of attorney under Part 1 of the Power of Attorney Act (short forms 1 and 2) lets an attorney do anything the donor can lawfully do by an attorney. It is not an enduring power of attorney, so it ends if the donor becomes mentally incapable, and also on death or revocation. Part 1 protects agents and third parties who act without knowing the authority has ended.

assigned.event: Donor signs a general power of attorney (Form 1 or 2 or other form)

starts.event: On signing, subject to any conditions in the document

ends.event: Donor becomes mentally incapable (not an enduring power of attorney)
Donor dies or revokes
Donor declared a patient by the court under the Patients Property Act

states.label: Authority ended by incapability, death, revocation or court declaration

transitions.event: Donor signs general power of attorney
Donor becomes mentally incapable
conditions: Rule comes from general agency law as described in official guidance; the Act defines only enduring powers as continuing during incapability

transitions.event: Court declares donor a patient
Donor dies
conditions: Acts by an agent without knowledge of termination remain valid for the agent and good-faith third parties (ss 3-4)

roles.name: Representative under a section 9 (non-standard) representation agreement
roles.summary: A capable adult can authorize a representative to make personal care and health care decisions, including where to live and giving or refusing life-sustaining treatment. The agreement takes effect on execution unless it names a later triggering event. The representative helps the adult decide or decides for the adult; the representative does not need a finding of incapacity. The agreement ends on the adult's death.

assigned.event: Adult who understands the nature and consequences signs a s 9 agreement before 2 witnesses (or 1 lawyer or notary); representative signs

starts.event: On execution unless the agreement names a later triggering event and says who confirms it. For substitute consent to health care, the health care provider must first be of the opinion that the adult is incapable of consenting.

ends.event: Adult dies
Capable adult revokes with written notice
Court cancels the agreement
Representative resigns, dies or becomes incapable, or spousal relationship ends (unless an alternate or co-representative continues, or the agreement says otherwise)
Adult becomes a patient by court order under the Patients Property Act (unless the court orders otherwise)

states.label: Executed but awaiting a stated triggering event
Representative may help make, or make, covered decisions
Suspended (e.g. a required monitor ceased to act, s 12(8))

transitions.event: Agreement executed (signed, witnessed, certificates completed) with no delayed trigger
conditions: Representative must sign before exercising authority

transitions.event: Agreement executed with a provision taking effect when an event occurs
conditions: Agreement must say how and by whom the event is confirmed

transitions.event: Triggering event confirmed
Adult becomes incapable
conditions: Authority not terminated solely by later incapability

transitions.event: Required monitor resigns, dies or becomes unable to act
conditions: Mainly for s 7(1)(b) financial provisions; lasts until a new monitor is appointed or the court dispenses with one

transitions.event: Capable adult revokes with written notice
Representative dies, resigns, becomes incapable, or spousal relationship ends
conditions: Not if another named representative may continue or an alternate is willing and able

transitions.event: Adult dies

notes.text: If the adult also has an advance directive, instructions in it about matters within the representative's authority are treated as the adult's capable wishes, unless the agreement lets the provider follow the directive directly.
Where a representation agreement and an enduring power of attorney conflict on financial matters, the enduring power of attorney prevails.

roles.name: Representative under a section 7 (standard) representation agreement
roles.summary: BC's supported decision-making tool. An adult can make a section 7 agreement even if unable to make a contract. It authorizes a representative to help the adult decide, or to decide for the adult, about personal care, routine finances, most health care and legal services. It cannot cover refusing life-preserving care. It takes effect on execution and ends on death.

assigned.event: Adult signs a s 7 agreement; the capacity test weighs relationship of trust and expressed wishes rather than contractual capacity

starts.event: On execution (all signatures, witnesses and certificates), unless a later triggering event is specified

ends.event: Adult dies
Revocation, court cancellation, or representative's death, resignation or incapability
Routine financial provisions cancelled on bankruptcy of the adult or representative, a receiver's appointment, or the representative's conviction for dishonesty

states.label: Representative helps the adult decide or decides for the adult on covered matters
Suspended while a required monitor is absent

transitions.event: Agreement executed
conditions: Each representative, and any required monitor, completes the prescribed certificate
Monitor required for routine financial provisions unless the representative is the spouse, PGT, trust company or credit union, or 2+ representatives must act unanimously

transitions.event: Representative consults the adult and follows current wishes where reasonable
Required monitor ceases to act
Bankruptcy of adult or representative, receiver appointed, or representative convicted of dishonesty offence (financial provisions only)
Adult dies

roles.name: Temporary substitute decision maker (TSDM)
roles.summary: If an adult who needs health care is found incapable of consenting and has no available personal guardian or representative with authority, the health care provider chooses the first qualified person on a statutory list (spouse, child, parent, sibling, grandparent, grandchild, other relative, close friend, relative by marriage), or someone authorized by the Public Guardian and Trustee. Authority is decision-specific and ends if the adult regains capability.

assigned.event: Health care provider decides the adult is incapable and chooses the first available qualified person in the s 16 order

starts.event: When chosen for a particular health care decision

ends.event: Adult becomes capable of giving or refusing consent
Person asks to be relieved and the provider chooses another person
Adult dies (no statutory post-death role; unverified as there is no express provision)

states.label: Chosen; may give or refuse substitute consent to the proposed health care

transitions.event: Provider chooses person under s 16
conditions: Adult has no available, capable personal guardian or representative with authority
Person is 19+, in contact with the adult in the last 12 months, has no dispute with the adult, is capable and willing to follow s 19 duties
PGT authorizes someone if nobody on the list qualifies or there is a dispute

transitions.event: Provider confirms in writing, no more than 21 days before care begins, that the adult is still incapable and the TSDM confirms care should begin
Adult regains capability
conditions: Decision rescinded; adult must consent before care begins or continues

transitions.event: TSDM asks to be relieved

notes.text: A TSDM may refuse life-preserving care only if the health care providers substantially agree that the refusal is medically appropriate and the TSDM followed s 19 duties. Some prescribed kinds of care are excluded.

A TSDM may apply for a personal guardian under the Adult Guardianship Act, and authority continues until a final order. That Act's Part 2 guardianship provisions are shown on bclaws as not in force, so in practice the court route is a Patients Property Act committee.

roles.name: Committee of the person (Patients Property Act)
roles.summary: On a court declaration, supported by 2 medical affidavits, that an adult cannot manage themself, the Supreme Court appoints a committee with custody of the person. The Public Guardian and Trustee is committee when no one else is appointed. The appointment terminates the adult's powers of attorney and, unless the court orders otherwise, their representation agreements. It ends when the court declares the person no longer incapable, or on discharge.

assigned.event: Supreme Court declares the adult incapable of managing himself or herself and appoints a committee (adult's own written nomination must be followed absent good reason)

ends.event: Court declares the patient no longer incapable (application after 1 year, or sooner by leave), then committee discharged
Court rescinds the appointment or appoints a successor committee
Patient dies: custody of the person has no further object; committee accounts to the executor or administrator and may be discharged

states.label: Committee has custody of the person

transitions.event: Court declaration and appointment
conditions: At least 10 days' personal notice to the adult unless dispensed with
Affidavits of 2 medical practitioners

transitions.event: Order declaring person no longer incapable; discharge
Patient dies

roles.name: Committee of the estate (Patients Property Act)
localNames: Public Guardian and Trustee as committee
roles.summary: A court-appointed committee for an adult declared incapable of managing their affairs. The committee has all the adult's rights and powers over the estate, except making a will. It must account to the Public Guardian and Trustee. After the patient's death, and until a representation grant is issued and served on it, the committee keeps its powers and also has a personal representative's powers.

assigned.event: Court declares adult incapable of managing affairs and appoints committee (or PGT by default)

starts.event: On the court order; any power of attorney terminates

ends.event: Court declares the person no longer incapable, then discharges the committee after accounts are passed
After death: when a representation grant has issued and written notice of it has been served on the committee (committee then accounts to the executor or administrator and may be discharged)

conditions: Court may restrict powers or require PGT consent

Representation grant issued and written notice served on committee
conditions: Committee must provide accounts to executor/administrator (or beneficiaries)

transitions.event: Declared no longer incapable; discharged

roles.name: Statutory property guardian (Public Guardian and Trustee by certificate of incapability)
roles.summary: An administrative route without a court. A qualified health care provider assesses the adult and reports to a health authority designate, who may issue a certificate of incapability after consulting the Public Guardian and Trustee (PGT) and notifying the adult and family. The PGT then becomes statutory property guardian. That suspends powers of attorney, which terminate if the PGT decides to manage the property.

assigned.event: Health authority designate issues a certificate of incapability

starts.event: As of the date the certificate is signed

ends.event: PGT satisfied the adult no longer needs a guardian and gives notice
Reassessment finds capability, accepted by health authority designate
Court ends it on review, or appoints a Patients Property Act committee
Adult dies: committee powers continue until a representation grant is served

transitions.event: Certificate of incapability issued
conditions: Adult needs decisions made, is incapable, will benefit, alternatives insufficient
No attorney with power over all financial affairs, or attorney not complying
No PPA committee exists

transitions.event: Capability found on reassessment, or PGT gives notice guardianship no longer needed
Court review ends guardianship or committee appointed

roles.name: Executor (grant of probate)
roles.summary: The executor named in a will gets authority from the will at death, and the estate vests in the executor on assuming office. To deal with most assets the executor applies to the Supreme Court for a grant of probate. The executor must first deliver notice (Form P1) to beneficiaries and others, then wait at least 21 days. The grant gives exclusive authority, and the executor is finished when discharged by the court.

starts.event: At death (executor assumes office; estate vests); exclusive authority confirmed by grant of probate after the notice period

ends.event: Appointment revoked before death because will-maker and executor-spouse ceased to be spouses (unless contrary intention in will)
Renunciation, or death before probate / failure to appear (forfeiture)
Removal or passing over by court, or revocation of grant
Court order discharging the personal representative after accounts

states.label: Named in an unrevoked will; will-maker living

Notice delivered; waiting 21 days, then application for estate grant filed
Grant of probate issued; exclusive authority; 210-day distribution restriction applies

Will-maker and named executor-spouse cease to be spouses before death
conditions: Subject to contrary intention in the will; reconciliation does not revive

transitions.event: Will-maker dies and executor assumes office
Executor delivers notice of proposed application (Form P1) and will copy

Diligent search for assets; affidavit of assets and liabilities

Court discharges personal representative
conditions: Without notice if accounts passed or all beneficiaries consented

roles.name: Administrator (grant of administration, with or without will annexed)
roles.summary: If there is no will, or no executor who can or will act, the court grants administration by statutory priority. For intestacy the order is spouse, then a child with the consent of a majority of children, then other intestate successors, then anyone the court considers appropriate, including the PGT. An intestate administrator is deemed personal representative from the date of death.

assigned.event: Court grants administration following the s 130 or s 131 priority list, or special-circumstances appointment

starts.event: On issue of the grant (estate vests in the court until then); for intestacy the administrator is conclusively deemed personal representative from the date of death

ends.event: Grant revoked, or administrator removed
Court discharge

states.label: Notice delivered (21-day wait); application filed; security if required

transitions.event: Applicant with priority delivers notice and applies
conditions: At least 21 days after notice
Security only if a minor or mentally incapable person without a nominee is interested, or the court requires it

transitions.event: Grant of administration issued
Discharge by court

notes.text: While a will contest or grant proceeding is pending, the court can appoint an administrator with full powers except distribution.

roles.name: Person consenting to post-mortem tissue gift (Human Tissue Gift Act)
localNames: person lawfully in possession of the body
roles.summary: BC uses opt-in consent. A person 19 or older can consent in writing, or orally before 2 witnesses during a last illness, and that consent binds after death. Without it, consent can come from, in order: spouse, adult child, parent, adult sibling, other adult next of kin, then the person lawfully in possession of the body. Nobody may consent if there is reason to believe the deceased would have objected.

assigned.event: No consent by the person; the first readily available person in the s 5 order is entitled

starts.event: On death, or when a medical practitioner believes death is imminent and the person cannot consent

ends.event: Tissue removed or the gift cannot be used (body then dealt with as if no consent)
Known objection by the deceased or a person of the same or closer relationship

Consent acted on, barred by objection, or window closed

transitions.event: Person's own s 4 consent governs on death
conditions: Must not act if reason to believe consent withdrawn, unless consent is in a valid will

transitions.event: Imminent death or death without own consent
conditions: Consent in writing, orally before 2 witnesses, or recorded message

transitions.event: Actual knowledge of objection by deceased or equal/closer relative

roles.name: Person with right to control disposition of remains
localNames: person with the right to control the disposition
personal representative named in the will
roles.summary: The right to control disposition of human remains passes in this order: the personal representative named in the will, spouse, adult child, adult grandchild, guardian (for a minor), parent, adult sibling, adult nephew or niece, adult next of kin, the ministry or PGT, then another adult with a personal relationship. Written preferences in a will or preneed contract bind that person unless unreasonable. Funeral providers need that person's written authorization.

assigned.event: Will names a personal representative, or by statutory order at death

ends.event: Remains disposed of
Person unavailable or unwilling: right passes to next in priority

notes.text: Top priority goes to the personal representative named in the will, not to a representative under a representation agreement or an attorney. Those roles end at death.

roles.name: Person who may act for a deceased individual under BC privacy law
roles.summary: Public bodies such as health authorities fall under FIPPA. There, a committee acting under Patients Property Act s 24, otherwise the personal representative, otherwise the nearest relative, may make access requests and give consents for a deceased adult. Private organizations such as private clinics fall under PIPA. There, the personal representative acts, including an executor named in the will before any grant, otherwise the nearest relative.

assigned.event: Status under statute or regulation at death (committee, personal representative, or nearest relative)

ends.event: A higher-ranked person (committee or personal representative) exists or becomes available, or the nearest relative ceases to be willing and able (passes to next)
PIPA: information about someone dead 20 or more years may be disclosed for archival or historical purposes without consent

states.label: May exercise the deceased's access and consent rights

transitions.event: Death; person is highest-ranked available
conditions: FIPPA: committee under PPA s 24, then personal representative, then nearest relative (spouse, adult child, parent, adult sibling, other relative, relative by marriage)

transitions.event: Nearest relative stops being willing or able

poaDurableByDefault.note: A power of attorney is enduring only if it states that authority continues despite incapability, and whether it may be used while the adult is capable or only while incapable. A general power of attorney ends on the donor's mental incapability.

springingPoaAllowed.note: An enduring power of attorney may take effect on a stated date or on a confirmed event, including incapability. The document must say how and by whom the event is confirmed. A qualified health care provider may confirm incapability if the named person cannot. Representation agreements can also have delayed triggers.

poaRegistrationBeforeUse.note: No registration with a government registry is needed before use. The attorney must sign before acting. For land, the enduring power of attorney must be executed and witnessed under the Land Title Act.

healthAgentStartsOn.note: A representation agreement takes effect on execution unless it names a later event. Representatives may act while the adult is capable, helping them decide. Substitute consent to a particular health care decision still requires the provider's opinion that the adult is incapable of consenting (HCCCFAA ss 7, 11).

supportedDecisionMakingStatute.name: Representation Agreement Act, RSBC 1996, c 405 (section 7 standard agreements)
supportedDecisionMakingStatute.note: Section 7 agreements let a representative help the adult make decisions, and can be made by an adult who cannot make a contract. The year is left null: the Act comes into force by regulation (s 45), and the original enactment and commencement dates were not verified on bclaws.

digitalAssetsFiduciaryStatute.note: No BC statute on fiduciary access to digital assets was found on bclaws. BC has not enacted the ULCC Uniform Access to Digital Assets by Fiduciaries Act (2016). Personal representatives rely on general authority under WESA s 142, and attorneys on Power of Attorney Act s 20(6) (delivery of property on request).

onlineToolsRecognisedInLaw.note: No BC enactment recognizes platform online-tool designations (e.g. legacy contacts).

organDonationModel.name: Human Tissue Gift Act, RSBC 1996, c 211
organDonationModel.note: Express consent by the donor (s 4), or by relatives in statutory order (s 5). There is no deemed consent.

smallEstateWithoutGrant.note: WESA Part 6, Division 2 (ss 109-120, small estate administration) is shown on bclaws as not in force. No statutory small-estate procedure without a grant is in force. The Probate Fee Act waives probate fees where the estate's value does not exceed $25 000, but a grant is still needed. All grant applications need notice at least 21 days before applying (Rule 25-2(2.1)).

probateGrantName.note: WESA also uses 'grant of administration' (with or without will annexed), collectively 'representation grant'. The Supreme Court Civil Rules use 'estate grant'.

deceasedPersonalDataProtected.note: Provincial privacy laws (FIPPA for public bodies, PIPA for private organizations) apply to deceased individuals' personal information. Regulations name who acts for the deceased, and PIPA permits archival disclosure after 20 years. Federal PIPEDA status is in ca-federal.

healthAgentPostDeathAuthority.note: Representation agreements and enduring powers of attorney end on death. The right to control disposition of remains goes to the personal representative named in the will, then family (CIFSA s 5). Exception on the property side: a Patients Property Act committee keeps its powers after the patient's death until a representation grant is served.
